chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Nasr via a chain of his own: From a man who dies and leaves dependents and has a debt, is money spent on them from his wealth? He said:
If he is certain that what is due [to creditors] encompasses all the wealth, then he should not spend on them; and if he is not certain, then he should spend on them from the middle of the wealth.

key_terms.عِيَالاً: dependents (family members supported by the deceased)
key_terms.وَسَطِ اَلْمَالِ: the middle of the wealth (typically interpreted as one-third)
key_terms.يُحِيطُ: encompasses/surrounds (referring to debt covering the entire estate)

ai.seo_question: How is a deceased person's estate distributed when they have both debts and dependents?
ai.summary: This ruling from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia juristic principle of prioritizing debt repayment over inheritance distribution, reflecting the Prophet's emphasis on settling obligations before bequests. The distinction between certainty and uncertainty in debt magnitude underscores the practical application of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) in estate liquidation, ensuring creditors' rights are protected while providing for dependents when assets are sufficient. This aligns with the broader Islamic legal maxim that 'the debt to Allah (debts) has more right to be settled.'
